lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Capital Cities: London and Islamabad
lesson.summary: Find out what a capital city is, visit London's landmarks and compare with Islamabad.
learning_objectives: Say what a capital city is

standards.text: Name and locate the capital cities of the UK; compare a small area of the UK with a non-European country

success_criteria: I can say what a capital city is
I can say how London and Islamabad are alike and different
lesson.real_life: Islamabad (Faisal Mosque, Pakistan Monument) and London (Elizabeth Tower, Tower Bridge), and British Pakistani families who commute.

warm_up.prompt: A river can flow through a city.
Which can we use to travel in a city?

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: what is a capital city?
blocks.say: Today we visit two big cities. One is in the UK and one is in Pakistan.

blocks.alt: Parliament buildings and a tall clock tower beside a river with a bridge and a small boat
blocks.caption: The Houses of Parliament, the clock tower and the River Thames in London.
blocks.credit: Photo by Ugur Akdemir on Unsplash
blocks.say: This is London, the capital of the UK. The clock tower is called Big Ben.

blocks.markdown: A **capital city** is the main city of a country.
blocks.say: A capital city is the main city of a country. The leaders work there.

blocks.markdown: The **government** makes decisions for a country.
blocks.say: The leaders are called the government. They make big decisions for everyone.

scenes.caption: London.
scenes.say: Every country has a capital city. The UK's capital is London.

scenes.caption: Islamabad.
scenes.say: Pakistan's capital is Islamabad.

scenes.caption: Government.
scenes.say: The government works in the capital. It makes rules and plans.

question.explanation: A capital is the main city of a country.

options.text: The main city of a country

blocks.say: Parliament is where people make laws for a country. London has a famous one.

blocks.alt: A modern white mosque with four tall minarets in front of green hills and a dark cloudy sky
blocks.caption: The Faisal Mosque in Islamabad, with the Margalla Hills behind it.
blocks.credit: Photo by Qasim Nagori on Unsplash
blocks.say: Islamabad is Pakistan's capital. It sits at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

scenes.caption: London.
scenes.say: London has the Houses of Parliament and Big Ben.

scenes.caption: Islamabad.
scenes.say: Islamabad has the Faisal Mosque, one of the biggest mosques in the world.

scenes.caption: Both.
scenes.say: Both capitals have parks, roads and people from many places.

question.prompt: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan.
question.hint: It is near the Margalla Hills.

blocks.title: Aisha's postcard
blocks.transcript: Aisha writes a postcard in Islamabad. On the front is the Faisal Mosque. Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan. The postcard flies to London on a plane. London is the capital of the UK. Her cousin sees Big Ben by the River Thames. He rides a red double-decker bus. Two capitals, two sets of landmarks, and one postcard.
blocks.caption: Aisha follows a postcard from Islamabad to London and spots Faisal Mosque and Big Ben.

points: A capital is the main city
blocks.say: Let us remember. A capital is the main city. The government works there.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Big Ben and the Thames

blocks.markdown: A **landmark** is a famous, easy-to-spot place.
blocks.say: A landmark is a famous place that is easy to spot. Big Ben is one.
The River Thames flows through London. Boats and bridges cross it.

scenes.caption: Big Ben.
scenes.say: Big Ben is the great bell in the tall clock tower.

scenes.caption: The Thames.
scenes.say: The Thames is a wide river. Many bridges cross it.

scenes.caption: Tower Bridge.
scenes.say: Tower Bridge has two towers and opens for tall ships.

blocks.markdown: A **palace** is a very grand home.
blocks.say: Buckingham Palace is where the King and Queen stay in London.

blocks.markdown: Landmarks help us find our way.
blocks.say: Look for the guards in red coats and tall black hats.

scenes.caption: The palace.
scenes.say: Buckingham Palace is a very big home with a wide front gate.

scenes.caption: Islamabad.
scenes.say: In Islamabad, we can see the Pakistan Monument and the Faisal Mosque.

scenes.caption: A clue.
scenes.say: Each landmark helps us tell which city we are in.

blocks.title: London or Islamabad?
blocks.goal: Move each landmark. Big Ben goes in London. The Faisal Mosque goes in Islamabad.
blocks.say: Sort the landmarks. Is each one in London or in Islamabad?

instructions: Draw it big, with its colours.
Say which city it is in.

points: A landmark is famous and easy to spot
blocks.say: Let us remember. Landmarks are famous places. Big Ben is in London.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Buses, the Tube and trains

blocks.alt: A red double-decker bus driving over Tower Bridge on a sunny day
blocks.caption: A red double-decker bus crossing Tower Bridge in London.
blocks.credit: Photo by Dawid Tkocz on Unsplash
blocks.say: People in big cities use buses, trains and the Tube to get around.
The Tube is the underground train. It runs below the ground in London.

scenes.caption: Bus.
scenes.say: A double-decker bus has two floors. You can sit upstairs.

scenes.caption: Tube.
scenes.say: The Tube runs under the ground, so it is fast.

scenes.caption: Train.
scenes.say: Trains carry people between towns and cities.

question.explanation: The Tube is London's underground railway.

blocks.markdown: To **commute** means to travel to work or school each day.
blocks.say: A commuter travels to work or school every day. Many use buses and trains.

blocks.title: City transport
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Warm up your memory. Watch the transport pictures light up, then copy them.

scenes.caption: Ways to commute.
scenes.say: Some commuters cycle. Some walk. Some take a bus or a train.

scenes.caption: Both cities.
scenes.say: In Lahore and London, many people ride buses to work.

scenes.caption: Clean air.
scenes.say: Sharing a bus is kinder to the air than many cars.

question.explanation: Commuters use many kinds of transport.

points: Cities have buses, trains and the Tube
A commuter travels to work or school
blocks.say: Let us remember. A commuter travels each day. Buses, trains and the Tube help.

blocks.markdown: A good plan has places, times and travel.
blocks.say: Let us plan a day out in London. First, pick three places to visit.

scenes.caption: Start.
scenes.say: Start at Big Ben. Then walk along the Thames.

scenes.caption: Bus.
scenes.say: Take a bus to Buckingham Palace.

scenes.caption: End.
scenes.say: End at Tower Bridge. Take the Tube home.

question.prompt: What do we pick first in a day-out plan?

blocks.markdown: To **compare** is to find the same and different.
blocks.say: Now compare London with Islamabad. How are they the same? How are they different?

scenes.caption: Same.
scenes.say: Same: both are capital cities with a government and parks.

scenes.caption: Different.
scenes.say: Different: London has the Tube. Islamabad is near the Margalla Hills.

scenes.caption: Landmarks.
scenes.say: Different: London has Big Ben. Islamabad has the Faisal Mosque.
